RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Jordan Jennings
Member ID: W990598603
Reference number: POC-3F7F71F65B-18736
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-08
Service: Bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296
Treating surgeon: Reyes, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Aetna Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 28296 (correction of hallux valgus with distal metatarsal osteotomy), as described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-08. The stated reason for denial was that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I respectfully disagree, and I ask that the determination be reversed based on the clinical record summarized below.

Governing policy

I understand this request was reviewed under Aetna's Clinical Policy Bulletin Number 0629, "Bunionectomy" (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0629.html). I was not able to independently confirm the "Last Review" or "Effective" date shown on that bulletin at the time of this letter, so I am not quoting or asserting a specific effective date; I ask Aetna to confirm which version of CPB 0629 was applied to my request and to identify the effective date of that version in its response.

CPB 0629 states, in the section addressing bony correction bunionectomy (which includes CPT 28296):

"Bony correction bunionectomy (e.g., Akin, Chevron, Keller, Lapidus, Mitchell, proximal metatarsal osteotomy procedures, etc.) to treat symptomatic hallux valgus (bunion) in a skeletally mature individual (i.e., after epiphyseal closure) or an individual who is 18 years of age or older when the following criteria is met: The member's pain and symptoms over the medial bony eminence or calluses persist, making walking difficult despite at least a 6-month trial of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional that includes the following: Protective cushions/pads; Shoe inserts (generally contractually excluded); Corticosteroid injections; Debridement of hyperkeratotic lesions; Oral analgesics or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs); Alternative or modified footwear that must include the following: Wearing well-fitting, low-heeled comfortable shoes made out of soft materials (e.g., canvas, cloth, soft leather) with wide toe box and padding; or Lace-ups or a combination last (front of the shoe is wider than the back of the shoe) that conforms to the bunion and minimizes irritation; and Radiographic confirmation of the most recent weight-bearing view X-ray demonstrating both of the following: An HVA of 30 degrees or greater; and An inter-metatarsal angle (IMA) (formed by the long axis of the first and second metatarsals) of 12 degrees or greater; and Documentation of skeletal maturity; and The member has one or more of the following: A neuroma secondary to the bunion; or Problems with a dorsiflexed second toe due to over-riding of the great toe (so-called cross-over toe deformity); or Limited or painful range of motion at the first toe MTP joint; or Painful prominence of the dorsiflexed second toe due to pressure from the first toe; or Ulceration caused by bunion; or Recurrent bursitis; or Demonstration of osteoarthritis on X-ray ... or The need for relief of a predisposing factor, e.g., Achilles tendon contracture."

The bulletin also states: "Radiographic confirmation must include interpretation and report of weight bearing anterior/posterior and lateral views of the affected foot."

Point-by-point response to the denial

1. Duration of symptoms and conservative treatment. My prior authorization packet documents 14 months of progressive foot pain unrelieved by rest — well beyond the 6-month trial referenced in the policy language quoted above.

2. Conservative treatment modalities. During that period I completed:
 - Activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic over 14 weeks (2026-03-21 to 2026-06-27), with 24 physical therapy visits completed and documented in the PT discharge note. This directly corresponds to the "Alternative or modified footwear" and "Shoe inserts" elements listed in the policy language above.
 - Oral NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, corresponding to the "Oral analgesics or non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs)" element quoted above.
 - A corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-14, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief, corresponding to the "Corticosteroid injections" element quoted above.
 Taken together, these modalities were administered under the direction of a healthcare professional over a period exceeding six months, consistent with the conservative-treatment requirement quoted above, and they failed to provide durable relief.

3. Radiographic findings. Weight-bearing foot radiographs dated 2026-06-23 show a hallux valgus angle (HVA) of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle (IMA) of 17 degrees. Both values exceed the thresholds stated in the policy language quoted above ("An HVA of 30 degrees or greater; and An inter-metatarsal angle (IMA) ... of 12 degrees or greater"). I ask Aetna to explain, in light of these specific values, why the reviewer concluded that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure," since the submitted films appear to meet the numerical thresholds set out in Aetna's own bulletin.

4. Additional qualifying clinical finding. The exam on file documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain at the first MTP joint. This corresponds to the "Limited or painful range of motion at the first toe MTP joint" criterion quoted above, which is one of the qualifying findings the policy requires in addition to the radiographic thresholds. In addition, the record documents that I cannot tolerate closed shoes and am at risk of skin breakdown over the prominence, which bears on the "Ulceration caused by bunion" and functional-impairment concerns addressed elsewhere in the same policy section.

5. Skeletal maturity and absence of exclusionary findings. I am an adult (skeletally mature), satisfying the "Documentation of skeletal maturity" element quoted above. The record also documents no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoker status — none of which correspond to any of the "not medically necessary" exclusions listed elsewhere in CPB 0629 (e.g., peripheral vascular disease, gangrene, non-ambulatory status, poor tissue at the operative site, or severe vascular insufficiency).

Requested action

Based on the above, the clinical record appears to satisfy each element of the bony-correction bunionectomy criteria quoted from CPB 0629: (a) more than six months of directed conservative treatment including footwear modification, orthotics, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injection; (b) weight-bearing radiographs showing HVA and IMA values above the stated thresholds; (c) a qualifying clinical finding of limited, painful first MTP joint range of motion; and (d) skeletal maturity with no applicable exclusion. I ask that Aetna:

1. Reverse the denial and authorize CPT 28296 as medically necessary; or
2. If Aetna maintains the denial, identify specifically which element(s) of CPB 0629's bony-correction bunionectomy criteria the reviewer found unmet, and provide the specific policy language and effective date relied upon, so that the record can be supplemented if needed; and
3. Arrange a peer-to-peer conversation between Dr. Reyes and the Aetna medical director who reviewed this request, given the specificity of the imaging findings at issue.

Enclosed with this appeal are: [list of enclosures — PT discharge note dated 2026-06-27; radiology report dated 2026-06-23; medication/injection records; office visit/exam notes; surgeon's letter of medical necessity from Dr. Reyes].

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-04 (180 days from the date of the denial notice), and I am submitting it well within that window. Please confirm receipt of this appeal in writing. If this internal appeal is not resolved in my favor, I intend to exercise my right to an independent external review, including through the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania's external review process, and I request that Aetna provide the applicable external review request form and instructions with any adverse determination on this appeal.

Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] with any questions or requests for additional documentation.

Sincerely,

Jordan Jennings
Member ID: W990598603
